title: Integer `//` has no domain error
verdict: no finding: only a zero divisor and `MIN // -1` fail
description: `//` on TINYINT, SMALLINT, INTEGER and BIGINT runs C++ `/` behind one wrapper, `BinaryNumericDivideWrapper`, instantiated per width. The wrapper has two failure paths: `MIN // -1` raises `Overflow in division` (duckdb-R1-min) and a zero divisor raises or gives NULL by `error_on_division_by_zero` (duckdb-R2). No other input fails, so no domain error occurs.
`/` of two integers is float division while `integer_division` is false (the default), which the lift reads as a `divide` of doubles.

evidence.note: BinaryNumericDivideWrapper: MIN / -1 raises, a zero divisor raises or sets NULL, else OP
INT8, INT16, INT32 and INT64 take the same wrapper

provenance.notes: One template for every width, so the reading covers i8 to i64.
